key_insight: CiteGuard-RAG shows that good retrieval is not enough for trustworthy QA: answers also need runtime validation to ensure every claim is grounded in cited evidence. By combining retrieval, citation constraints, and sentence-level checks, the system can produce more reliable answers and refuse unsupported ones.
problem_solved: Retrieval-augmented generation often returns fluent answers that are not fully supported by evidence, have invalid citations, or should have been refused. This paper addresses the gap between "finding relevant sources" and "producing citation-valid, grounded answers."
method: Uses hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval to collect relevant evidence.
Generates answers under citation constraints so claims must align with sources.
Performs sentence-level grounding validation at runtime and uses single-pass regeneration when validation fails.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the trustworthiness of RAG systems by reducing unsupported claims and citation errors. It is especially useful in high-stakes settings where factual accuracy, traceability, and appropriate refusal matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing retrieval -> generation -> validation -> regeneration/refusal.
Side-by-side example of grounded vs. ungrounded answer with highlighted citations.
Validation checklist icon set for sentence-level support, citation match, and refusal triggers.
Flowchart showing how hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval combines two evidence signals.
paper_title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
paper_authors: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong
